Article Title: IPL 2027: Steffan Jones joins Mumbai Indians as bowling consultant
Article Text:
Steffan Jones (Twitter Photo)

NEW DELHI: Steffan Jones, former high-performance coach at Rajasthan Royals (RR), will join Mumbai Indians (MI) as a bowling consultant for their development program, TimesofIndia.com has learnt.The 52-year-old will work with MI's development squad alongside Zubin Bharucha, who has joined the five-time champions as director of performance, earlier this year.Jones, who also served as Rajasthan Royals' fast-bowling coach during the 2019 edition of the IPL, was later brought back by the franchise as its high-performance fast-bowling coach ahead of IPL 2022.It is also learnt that Bharucha and Jones have a specific role: to work with Indian players during the ongoing domestic season.Jones, who played first-class cricket in the English county circuit between 1997 and 2011, recently worked with India all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy. The Welshman helped the youngster improve his bowling speed. Reddy, who used to bowl in the mid-120s, is now consistently clocking the mid-130s.Earlier on Saturday, MI roped in Kieron Pollard as their head coach, replacing Mahela Jayawardene . The franchise is likely to take the big call on captaincy and movement is expected on Hardik Pandya trade in the coming weeks.
Article Summary: Steffan Jones will join Mumbai Indians as a bowling consultant. 52-year-old will work with MI's development squad alongside Zubin Bharucha. Jones also served as Rajasthan Royals' fast-bowling coach during the 2019 edition of the IPL.

Article Title: Australian umpire's Ranji Trophy sojourn: Aeroplanes overhead at Palam, BKC's red soil pitch, love for garlic naan and vada pav
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Last week, when umpire Ben Treloar stepped out to officiate the Ranji Trophy match between Delhi and Gujarat at the Palam Air Force II Ground, he caught everyone's attention. Players from both sides were curious about the Australian umpire, with most approaching him on the opening day of the drawn fixture, in which Delhi secured the first-innings lead, to ask where he was from."Quite a few players asked me where I was from and what was going on. They were genuinely welcoming and interested," Treloar told TimesofIndia.com from Mumbai.The 44-year-old from Sydney is in India for the first time as part of the Umpire Exchange Program for the 2026-27 season between Cricket Australia and the Board of Control for Cricket in India ( BCCI ). As part of the programme, Australian umpire Ben Treloar will officiate in two Ranji Trophy matches in India, while Indian umpire Parashar Joshi will travel to Australia to stand in two Sheffield Shield matches and one One-Day Cup fixture."It's my first time in India, and I'm really enjoying the experience. Everything is brand new, and I'm experiencing it for the first time. At the end of the day, it's just another game of cricket, but one of the differences is that I don't know any of the players here, and they don't know me. We're all meeting for the first time."The similarity is the high standard of cricket. The players are incredibly talented, and the standard of first-class cricket here is very high.It's similar in Australia [in the Sheffield Shield], where we also have gifted players who perform at their best," he says."The other similarity is the passion with which the game is played. Players here and back in Australia play for their livelihoods. They play hard, play fair and compete in the right spirit. It's great to be out in the middle, be part of that and contribute to the game."The playing conditions are slightly different, particularly the session timings. The first session here lasts two and a half hours because play starts a little earlier, whereas in Australia, the first session is two hours before the lunch break. The number of overs is also different. Here, it's 90 overs a day, compared to 96 in Australia," he adds.For Treloar, who has been umpiring for the past 21 years, the most unique experience at Palam was the aeroplanes frequently flying over the ground."Palam was great. It's obviously a smaller venue, and there isn't as much infrastructure around the ground. There were aeroplanes flying overhead, probably one every five minutes across the four days. By the end of the match, you sometimes don't even realise a plane is coming because you get used to it," he says."But that doesn't change what we do out in the middle. It's another ground, another first-class match and another opportunity to officiate some really good cricket. What I noticed was how passionate everyone involved in the match was about cricket and providing excellent hospitality. From the caterers and ground staff to the players, team management and coaches, everyone was welcoming and made it a really good experience," he adds.Away from the field, Treloar works as Cricket New South Wales' Umpire Education Officer, helping develop the next generation of match officials. His contribution to umpire education has been recognised with four George Borwick Memorial Awards from the New South Wales Cricket Umpires and Scorers Association."I'm very grateful to both the BCCI and Cricket Australia for maintaining such a strong and positive relationship. The way they support match officials and provide them with these additional experiences is fantastic. We're very thankful for the opportunity, and I was honoured and proud to be offered the chance to come to India," he says.He will next umpire the third-round match between Mumbai and Haryana at Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) ground."I've had a quick look at the BKC ground in Mumbai, and it's a much more established venue. I'm really looking forward to getting out there in a couple of days and experiencing a different type of pitch. This one has red soil, so I anticipate it will offer a little more. We'll also spend some time watching the nets and getting a feel for the conditions before the match," he says of the BKC pitch.Apart from cricket and the contrasting soil types (black soil in Delhi and red soil in Mumbai), Treloar has been enjoying Indian cuisine and its flavours. He is also noting down recipes to take back home for his family."The food has been incredible. It's spicy, I must tell you. I do ask for mild food, but I've really embraced the cuisine in both Delhi and Mumbai. The food has been high quality, with so much flavour, and I'm really enjoying it."I particularly like the stuffed potatoes. I've been eating a lot of vegetarian food, and the dal, the quality of the breads, including roti and garlic butter naan, and the vegetable curries and vada pav have all been fantastic."When I get home, I'm looking forward to expanding my cooking abilities. I'll be cooking a lot more of these dishes for my family," he says.
Article Summary: Australian umpire Ben Treloar is in India for the first time as part of the Umpire Exchange Program for the 2026-27 season. He will officiate in two Ranji Trophy matches in India, while Indian umpire Parashar Joshi will travel to Australia to stand in two Sheffield Shield matches and one One-Day Cup fixture. The 44-year-old from Sydney is enjoying the high standard of cricket.

Article Title: India's para track and field stars lead golden surge at Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Dilip Mahadu Gavit (IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s para-athletes continued to swell the medal tally with a superb haul of gold medals on Thursday, as Shailesh Kumar spearheaded a podium sweep in the men’s high jump T63, Anjanaben Bumbadiya triumphed in the women’s 400m T47, and Dilip Mahadu Gavit secured his second gold of the Games in Nagoya.Defending champion Dharmaraj Solairaj smashed the Asian record in the men’s T44/T62/T64 long jump, while Suvarna Raj clinched gold in the women’s F54 discus throw, underlining the nation’s growing strength across para-athletics disciplines.Shailesh produced a Games-record leap of 1.89m to take the high jump gold. Former Paralympic bronze medallist Varun Bhati claimed silver with a season’s best of 1.84m, while Rahul completed the Indian clean sweep with 1.81m.Bumbadiya clocked 59.97s to win the women’s 400m T47 title, with compatriot Jayanti Behera taking silver in 1:00.65. Thailand’s Sasirawan Inthachot finished third in 1:02.58.Gavit, who had won the men’s 100m T47 gold on Wednesday, added another yellow metal by winning the 400m in 48.27s. Bhavikkumar Bharwad initially finished second in 49.31s but was disqualified for a second lane infringement. Japan’s Kakeru Ishida was consequently upgraded to silver, while Uzbekistan’s Marufjon Murodulloev took bronze.Solairaj, a 32-year-old Tamil Nadu jumper, registered 7.15m in his second attempt to break the Asian record. Malaysia’s Eddy Bernard won silver with 6.34m, while Japan’s Yuma Tamaki secured bronze with 6.89m.Suvarna, 44, delivered a winning discus throw of 15.66m. Iran’s Shahla Hadidi took silver with 15.45m and Vietnam’s Thi Ngoc Thuy Nguyen won bronze with 14.65m. India added further podium finishes through visually impaired Tejalben Damor, who won silver in the women’s 400m T12 in 57.60 seconds after her 200m bronze, and Ravanni Valasanaini, who claimed bronze in the women’s 400m T11 with a personal best of 1:03.64.India has so far won 52 medals from para-athletics, with 18 gold, 16 silver and 18 bronze after the end of Day 4 of the competitions.
Article Summary: Shailesh Kumar leads podium sweep in men's high jump T63. Anjanaben Bumbadiya wins women's 400m T47 title. Dilip Mahadu Gavit secures his second gold of the Games in Nagoya.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sandeep, Haney strike gold with world-record feats as India hit 100 medals
Article Text:
Sandeep sets T44 world record (Image: ANI)

Sandeep sets world record, Ajay Kumar claims bronze

Haney breaks world record with 60.49m javelin throw

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India reach 100-medal milestone

India's golden run at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games gathered further momentum on Friday as Sandeep and Haney clinched gold medals with world-record performances in their respective events, taking the country's overall medal tally to 100. Sandeep set a new world record in the men's 400m T64, while Haney produced a record-breaking throw in the men's javelin F37/38 final at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium.Sandeep clocked 52.28 seconds to win the men's 400m final, finishing comfortably ahead of Saudi Arabia's Nour Alsana, who secured silver in 53.13 seconds, a season's best. India's Ajay Kumar claimed bronze in 53.61 seconds, setting a Games record, while China's Huang Ruihua finished fourth with a personal-best time of 54.39 seconds.In the men's 400m, athletes from the T44 and T64 classifications competed together. While Sandeep and Alsana belong to the T44 category, Ajay Kumar competes in T64. Both classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments.Haney followed with a world-record throw of 60.49 metres to claim gold in the men's javelin F37/38 event, earning 1,116 Raza points. Iran's Hormoz Seidikazpounji took silver with a personal-best throw of 50.68 metres, earning 1,009 points, while China's Yu Chengjie secured bronze with an Asian-record effort of 53.66 metres and 943 points.The combined F37 and F38 javelin categories are decided using Raza points, which account for the different classifications. This explains why Seidikazpounji finished ahead of Yu despite recording a shorter throw.The double world-record triumph marked another significant milestone for India, whose overall medal tally crossed 100 at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games.
Article Summary: India reach 100-medal milestone at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games. Sandeep and Haney clinch gold medals with world-record performances in their respective events, taking the country's overall medal tally to 100. Haney breaks world record with 60.49m javelin throw.

Article Title: India tour of New Zealand: Red-hot Shikhar Mohan earns India A call-up; set to replace KL Rahul for two fixtures
Article Text:
Shikhar Mohan (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan has received a maiden India A call-up for the last two four-day matches against New Zealand. The 21-year-old will replace KL Rahul, who will join the ODI squad after playing the first four-day match against New Zealand A, starting on Saturday at Bert Sutcliffe Oval at Lincoln University.The southpaw has continued his red-hot form with back-to-back hundreds in the ongoing Ranji Trophy season. Shikhar smashed 143 against Kerala in Jamshedpur and then scored a match-saving 127 against Maharashtra in Pune.Shikhar's mentor, Ishank Jaggi, a former Jharkhand cricketer, has heaped praise on the youngster, saying the time is absolutely ripe for him to take the next step."It is perfect timing. He is in good form. Scored two centuries in Ranji. Had a great Duleep Trophy final and Irani Trophy as well," Jaggi told TimesofIndia.com.After an excellent debut season in 2025-26, in which he amassed 613 runs at an average of 55.73, including two centuries, he has started the new season in rollicking fashion, smashing 143 in Jharkhand's opening match against Kerala at the Keenan Stadium in Jamshedpur.The southpaw also made some valuable contributions in the Duleep Trophy final for East Zone, scoring 85 and 52 in the two innings, followed by a solid 60 on a green top in Srinagar in the Irani Trophy, playing for Rest of India against defending Ranji Trophy champions Jammu and Kashmir.Jaggi, who is currently coaching the Jharkhand U-23 side, says Shikhar Mohan has been in top form for the past four to five years."Look, he has been in good form for the last four to five years. He has dominated age-group cricket as well. I feel this is a great time for him to have this experience. It will be great exposure for him. He will realise what he needs to add to his game and will come back as a better cricketer," says Jaggi, who has played 90 First Class matches.Jaggi is correct about the southpaw's rich vein of form. Shikhar Mohan enjoyed significant success with the Under-23 side in the Col CK Nayudu Trophy. In the 2023-24 season, he scored 623 runs, including two hundreds and three fifties. He continued his run-scoring spree the following season, scoring 887 runs, which helped him earn a call-up to the senior side.One issue with Shikhar's batting, which the youngster himself has admitted to, is his inability to convert starts into big scores, something he is working on with Jaggi."In my first year of Under-19 cricket, I scored around 550 runs, with most of my scores in the 70s and 80s. The following year, I wanted to focus more and convert those starts into bigger scores," he had told this website."Before facing a ball, I talk to myself. I remind myself to watch the ball and stay focused. That has helped me a lot. Jaggi bhai also helped me with this, especially when he was with the Under-19 team. I started concentrating more and focusing on one ball at a time.That approach has really helped me," he added.Ishank, however, feels the mental block is something even the game's greats have faced."Everyone has gone through that phase. But you have to understand that he is scoring those 70s and 80s consistently, which is no small achievement. He is still raw and can be groomed, and that's why I said this call has come at the right time," he said.Shikhar will travel to New Zealand on October 26 and will link up with the India A squad in Christchurch, where the second four-day game will be played from October 31.
Article Summary: Jharkhand opener Shikhar Mohan has received a maiden India A call-up for the last two four-day matches against New Zealand. The 21-year-old will replace KL Rahul, who will join the ODI squad. The southpaw has continued his red-hot form with back-to-back hundreds in the ongoing Ranji Trophy season.

Article Title: With Brandon Royval setback behind him, Lone’er Kavanagh braces for Ramazan Temirov’s knockout threat at UFC 333
Article Text:
Lone’er Kavanagh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lone’er Kavanagh has not made major changes to his preparation for Ramazan Temirov. The British flyweight says the work has centred on mistakes from his last fight, a submission loss to Brandon Royval in July.“There hasn't been too much change. It's more about learning from the mistakes I made in the last fight,” Kavanagh told TimesofIndia.com ahead of his UFC 333 fight on October 24 at the Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. “I have such a good team around me that we're always evolving and working on the finer details - the little things we need to improve.”Kavanagh, ranked sixth in the UFC flyweight division, faces 10th-ranked Temirov. The fight comes after a year in which he beat former champion Brandon Moreno by unanimous decision in February before losing to Royval in July. Both bouts went beyond the opening round, but ended differently for the 27-year-old.“Both fights have taught me a lot, and I'm going to continue learning from them,” Kavanagh said. “Every fight I have and every mistake I make will teach me something until the day I retire. I think that's the main thing - I'm always learning.”The Moreno fight was a five-round test against a former champion, while Royval submitted Kavanagh with a rear-naked choke in the third round. The latter bout also earned both fighters Fight of the Night honours. Kavanagh now returns to the Octagon against an opponent coming off a first-round knockout.Temirov stopped former flyweight title challenger Steve Erceg in July, extending his winning streak to 12 fights. The Uzbek fighter has a 20-3 professional record, including 12 knockout wins and 11 first-round finishes.“Obviously, Ramazan is very powerful. He likes to come forward and land big shots, and I feel like that works very well for me,” Kavanagh said. “As long as I stay focused and switched on, I'm able to make it a good fight and keep myself safe.”Temirov called out Kavanagh after the Erceg victory. The Englishman, however, sees little reason to read a personal motive into the challenge.“I think it's just a fight that makes sense, right? Obviously, he wants to climb up the rankings, and I was next on the ladder,” Kavanagh said. “So I don't take it personally because I do the same thing. I'm always looking to climb upwards.”The rankings give the bout a clear purpose. Kavanagh is looking to consolidate his position after the Royval defeat, while Temirov has the chance to beat a top-six opponent after his win over Erceg. For Kavanagh, the immediate target is to establish himself as a future title contender.“I think it's a good fight to establish myself as a future title contender,” he said. “He's got a good record and is coming off a good win, so I feel like the winner will be right back at the top.”He is not ready to name a preferred opponent beyond Saturday. Kavanagh said he would speak to his coach and manager after the fight before deciding on his next move.“I'm not too sure yet. I'm very much a one-fight-at-a-time kind of person,” he said. “So, I'll get this one done first, then we'll speak to my coach and my manager and see what's next.”Asked what version of himself fans should expect to see against Temirov, Kavanagh returned to the idea of continued improvement.“The best version of myself - the one that's always improving,” he said. “And, yeah, that's what's going to happen.”UFC 333 will be live on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.
Article Summary: Lone’er Kavanagh has not made major changes to his preparation for Ramazan Temirov. The British flyweight says the work has centred on mistakes from his last fight, a submission loss to Brandon Royval in July. The fight comes after a year in which he beat former champion Brandon Moreno by unanimous decision.

Article Title: Qatar to host FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2026 final as PSG await continental challengers
Article Text:
FIFA Intercontinental Cup (Pic credit: FIFA)

Three decisive matches in Qatar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mamelodi Sundowns advance after defeating Al Ahli

Qatar will host the final three matches of the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2026, with the tournament culminating in the final on December 16, when defending champions Paris Saint-Germain will take on the FIFA Challenger Cup winners.FIFA has confirmed that the concluding fixtures of the annual club competition will be played on December 9, 12 and 16, bringing together continental champions from across the six confederations in the race for the title. This will be the third consecutive year that Qatar has hosted the final stages, following the 2024 and 2025 editions.The FIFA Derby of the Americas and FIFA Challenger Cup will be staged at Jassim bin Hamad Stadium in Doha, while Ahmad bin Ali Stadium in Al Rayyan will host the final.PSG, who won the competition in Qatar in December 2025, will enter the final as defending champions after Real Madrid lifted the trophy in the inaugural edition under the current format in 2024.The FIFA Derby of the Americas will open the Qatar leg on Wednesday, December 9, with Toluca FC, the Concacaf Champions Cup winners, facing the winners of the 2026 CONMEBOL Libertadores at Jassim bin Hamad Stadium.The victors will return to the same venue on Saturday, December 12, to meet African champions Mamelodi Sundowns FC in the FIFA Challenger Cup.The winner of that contest will secure a place in the final against PSG on Wednesday, December 16.The competition features five single-leg matches in total, with the opening two fixtures taking place at the home stadiums of participating clubs as determined by FIFA rankings. The final three matches will be played in Qatar, with four trophies available across the tournament.The 2026 competition began in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, on August 26, when AFC Champions League winners Al Ahli FC defeated OFC Champions League winners Auckland FC 1-0 in the FIFA African-Asian-Pacific Play-off.CAF Champions League winners Mamelodi Sundowns then beat Al Ahli FC 2-1 in Pretoria, South Africa, on September 19, winning the FIFA African-Asian-Pacific Cup and booking their place in the FIFA Challenger Cup.Sundowns will now await the winner of the Derby of the Americas for a shot at reaching the final.With PSG already assured of a place in the title decider, the three December fixtures in Qatar will determine which clubs from the Americas and Africa progress to challenge the European champions for the 2026 crown.
Article Summary: Qatar will host the final three matches of the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2026. The final three fixtures of the club competition will be played on December 9, 12 and 16. This will be the third consecutive year that Qatar has hosted the final stages, following the 2024 and 2025 editions. The FIFA Derby of the Americas and FIFA Challenger Cup will be staged at Jassim bin Hamad Stadium in Doha, while Ahmad bin Ali Stadium in Al Rayyan willhost the final.

Article Title: No sponsor, a career-threatening setback and one big dream: Nayanika Sanga’s story
Article Text:
Nayanika Sanga (Insta)

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Nayanika Sanga, golf has always been about more than the scorecard. As the 22-year-old from Gurugram prepares to compete at the Women’s Indian Open from Oct 22-25 at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, she is drawing on lessons learnt over years of competition, international exposure and a difficult comeback from injury. Her approach is simple: concentrate on what she can control, appreciate the opportunity to play and treat every round as a fresh challenge.The philosophy reflects a maturity that has developed through experience. Having travelled abroad for tournaments, including competing in France, Nayanika has learnt to approach the demands of professional golf with greater perspective.“When you play in India, it is like a family. You feel at home and at ease. But when you play outside, the environment is different. People are new, and there can be a language barrier. I think that has made me a little more resilient. When I compete back home now, I feel comfortable because I know the place and the people,” she said.Her journey began when she was five. Her father, who serves in the Navy, wanted her to take up a sport, believing it would help her develop as an individual. She tried squash, tennis and golf, but the response to her natural ability with a club encouraged the family to pursue the latter.Competition soon followed, and the game became a defining part of her life.One of the earliest milestones arrived when she was 11, winning the Kazi Cup at Willingdon Club in Mumbai.“That was definitely a life-changing experience because that was my first win as a child, a big win as a child. Once you start winning, it reinforces that feeling that you want to keep chasing it again and again,” she said.The road since then, however, has not been without setbacks. A wrist injury four years ago came at a particularly difficult time, when she had just turned professional and was playing well. Gratitude journalling became an important part of that process.“When I started playing again, I began focusing on smaller things and feeling grateful that at least today I can play, and tomorrow I can compete. Instead of thinking, ‘I need to win today’, being grateful for the small things in life has definitely helped me,” she said.Physical conditioning has also played a significant role in her return. A professional golfer’s workload extends beyond the hours spent practising and playing. Frequent travel, tournaments scheduled close together and the physical demands of carrying her own bag at overseas events can take a toll. Nayanika credits her strength and conditioning coach, Shaurya Sinha, with helping her rebuild confidence in her body and handle the demands of the circuit.“Because of fitness, I have been a little more resilient to injuries. Other than the injury I had four years ago, I have not had any issues, and I feel my fitness routine is what gets me going every week,” she said.The Women’s Indian Open will present another test. Nayanika regards the DLF Golf and Country Club course as challenging, but prefers to see its demands as an opportunity rather than an obstacle.“I think it is challenging in a fun way. I do not see the course as challenging; rather, every day will be a new challenge there. It will be fun to tackle a new challenge every day,” she said.That outlook also shapes how she approaches a field featuring accomplished players. Rather than becoming preoccupied with the reputations of her opponents, she wants to learn from them while remaining focused on her own performance. She relies more on feel and instinct than data when making decisions on the course, trusting her judgement when she believes her game is in good shape.Nayanika has also witnessed the growth of women’s golf in India. When she first turned professional, she recalled fields of around 30 to 35 players. This year, she said, the numbers have risen to approximately 60 to 62, reflecting greater interest among younger golfers in pursuing the professional route. Lower scores and more opportunities to compete overseas have contributed to the improving standard.Yet the growth of the game has not removed one of its persistent challenges: funding. Despite competing abroad and continuing to develop as a professional, she is still looking for a sponsor. Coming from a middle-class family, with her father serving in the Navy, she knows the financial demands of sustaining a career on tour.“It has been tough. My parents have sacrificed so much for me, and they continue to do so to support me,” she said.Her grandparents also travelled with her to tournaments when she was younger, stepping in whenever her father’s work commitments prevented him from accompanying her. Nayanika acknowledges their contribution.Away from golf, time with friends and playing badminton help her switch off from the constant demands of professional competition. She also looks up to Diksha Dagar and Aditi Ashok whose achievements have out Indian golf on the global map.Nayanika hopes her journey can encourage more young girls to pursue sport, particularly in a society where conventional career choices often dominate expectations.“If you fall in love with a sport, there is nothing better than that feeling. Parents should be willing to explore sporting opportunities when their children show interest and ability,” she said.As she heads into the Women’s Indian Open, her ambitions remain tied to the fundamentals she has learnt through experience: trust her instincts, stay patient and focus on the next shot. For a golfer who has learnt to find perspective in adversity, the challenge is not simply to compete against a strong field, but to keep moving forward, one round at a time.
Article Summary: Nayanika Sanga, 22, will compete at the Women’s Indian Open from Oct 22-25 at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram. Her approach is simple: concentrate on what she can control, appreciate the opportunity to play and treat every round as a fresh challenge.

Article Title: Three Jharkhand players in India squad for historic lawn bowls series against New Zealand
Article Text:
(From left) Sunil Bahadur, Dinesh Kumar and Reshma Kumari

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kolkata: Three players from Jharkhand will be part of India’s four-member lawn bowls squad for a historic three-Test series against New Zealand in Nov, part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two countries.Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme.2022 Commonwealth Games silver medallists Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur and rising player Reshma Kumari, all from Jharkhand, have been selected alongside Arjuna Awardee and Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki Singh for the series, scheduled from Nov 16-18 in Auckland.“This is a very important event for us because only four sports are taking part in the centenary celebrations. On the days we are playing, no other sport will be taking place, which means we will receive exclusive coverage,” Bowling Federation of India president Ravi Bengani told TOI in an exclusive interview on Thursday.India will play three Test matches over three days, with each Test comprising five matches — men’s pairs, women’s pairs, mixed fours, mixed pairs 1 and mixed pairs 2.The New Zealand series is part of a broader international exposure programme the federation has put in place as it begins preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.A 12-member Indian contingent will travel to Malaysia later this month for a World Bowls-sanctioned tournament, while another group will compete in an invitational event in Hong Kong, where Indian players won bronze medals last year.The federation’s confidence has also received a boost from Putul Sonowal’s recent podium finish at the Champion of Champions event, a first for an Indian player at the prestigious competition.“We have decided to participate in as many World Bowls-sanctioned events as possible. International exposure is crucial if we want to bridge the gap with the leading nations,” Bengani said.The federation is also planning to strengthen its support structure through its partnership with Bowls New Zealand. Bengani revealed that India currently does not have a dedicated national coach, making the proposed knowledge-sharing programme particularly significant.“We have signed an agreement with Bowls New Zealand and now we will have more exchange programmes. We will bring their coaches and technical officials to India and provide our players with greater exposure and expertise,” Bengani said.The plans have gained momentum following the federation’s recognition by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports earlier this year, a move expected to improve funding and access to high-performance support.As far as the 2030 Commonwealth Games are concerned, the federation has set ambitious targets. “I’m committing to at least four gold medals for India in 2030. Personally, I feel we can win even more if we continue on the current path,” Bengani said.With a packed international calendar, plans to bring in New Zealand coaches and technical experts, and Ahmedabad 2030 on the horizon, the federation believes Indian lawn bowls is entering its most ambitious phase yet.

Article Title: EFI mess costs Indian riders global stage, FEI ban from Dec 1
Article Text:
Equestrian Federation of India

New Delhi:

Yet another tale of administrative chaos and athletes paying the price. Caught in a prolonged governance crisis at the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes’ exposure to global competition.The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections, effectively shutting Indian riders, officials, trainers and horses out of international events. TOI is in possession of FEI’s Oct 15 letter confirming the decision, which was taken at the international body's board meeting on Oct 13.Explaining its move, the FEI said the EFI’s prolonged governance crisis had reached a tipping point. “The absence of elections to date to elect a new Executive Committee, has resulted in a prolonged governance and leadership irregularity that is no longer sustainable,” the letter by FEI Governance Director Francisco Lima stated.The crisis follows the Delhi high court’s dissolution of the EFI executive committee in Feb 2026. Its elected tenure had expired in Sept 2023, while fresh elections remain pending nine months after the court’s intervention. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) constituted an ad hoc committee on March 27 to oversee the federation and facilitate the electoral process.While acknowledging the committee’s Sept 27 submission and its work, the FEI said elections were expected by Jan 31, 2027. However, the suspension will be reviewed only after the polls are held and evaluated by the international body.The consequences are sweeping. Citing its statutes, the FEI said the EFI “may not attend or be represented at any session or meeting of any FEI body, nor may it organise international events.” More damagingly, athletes, officials, trainers and horses “may not participate in international events organised by the FEI or any other national federation, whether under the Indian flag or the FEI flag.”With the suspension taking effect before the stated election deadline, Indian riders risk losing crucial international competition opportunities. Their return will depend on the completion of elections and the FEI’s subsequent evaluation, leaving athletes caught in a governance crisis they did not create.
Article Summary: The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections. Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes' exposure to global competition.

Former Australia captain Steve Smith has been cleared of concussion and resumed fielding duties on the fifth day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead in Durban on Tuesday, after undergoing a series of clinical assessments following a blow to the helmet.The 37-year-old batter was struck by a short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje during Australia's second innings. Smith attempted to duck under the ball but misjudged its trajectory as it failed to rise as much as he expected.Although he continued batting after the incident, scoring 27 off 41 balls before being caught at long-on off Simon Harmer, Smith did not take the field when South Africa began their second innings on Monday. Michael Neser served as his substitute fielder during that session.However, Smith returned to the field on Tuesday morning after being cleared under Cricket Australia's concussion protocols. He was stationed in the slip cordon when South Africa resumed their chase and subsequently took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling."Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning," Cricket Australia said in a statement.The incident brought back memories of Smith's previous concussion scare during the 2019 Ashes in England, when he was struck on the head by fast bowler Jofra Archer and forced to miss part of a Test match.Smith's return to the field came after medical assessments over the preceding 24 hours, with Australia following the prescribed protocols before allowing the experienced batter to resume his duties.His presence was a boost for Australia as they pushed for victory in the series opener, with South Africa mounting a determined resistance on the final day.South Africa resumed at 102/4 on Tuesday, needing another 319 runs to win. They reached 166/6 by lunch after Australia struck twice to strengthen their grip on the contest.Opener Aiden Markram led the home side's resistance, remaining unbeaten on 69 at the interval alongside Marco Jansen on seven. The pair had to rebuild after Wiaan Mulder's patient 69-run fifth-wicket partnership with Markram ended when Josh Hazlewood had Mulder caught behind by Alex Carey.Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw then dismissed Verreynne, who made just one before edging a reckless shot to Smith at slip.Renshaw has been Australia's standout performer with the bat, having scored 190 in the first innings and 82 in the second, before adding two wickets to his match contribution.Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test. The second Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Gqeberha on Sunday.

Smith took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling. Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test.

NEW DELHI: India A recovered from a difficult start to the match with three late wickets, but New Zealand A finished Day 1 of the first unofficial Test in a strong position at 135/3, leading by 22 runs.India A were bowled out for just 113 in their first innings after struggling against the New Zealand A pace attack. The hosts then built a solid opening partnership of 132 runs before Mukesh Choudhary dismissed captain Rhys Mariu for 76.Auqib Nabi struck twice in successive deliveries towards the end of the day to remove nightwatchman Jayden Lennox and Tim Robinson for ducks. His late strikes gave India A some momentum after a tough day with the ball.At stumps, Curtis Heaphy was unbeaten on 37, while Matthew Boyle was yet to score.India A struggled to build partnerships after being asked to bat in conditions that helped the fast bowlers. However, he ran out of partners as India A were dismissed in 39.3 overs.Simon Keene led New Zealand A's bowling effort with five wickets for 24 runs in 11.3 overs. Zak Gibson took three wickets for 29 runs, while Kristian Clarke and Fraser Sheat claimed one wicket each.New Zealand A made a steady start to their reply, with Mariu and Heaphy showing patience against India's pace attack.The openers put together a 132-run partnership. Mariu was the more attacking batter, scoring 76 off 137 balls with 12 fours, while Heaphy remained solid at the other end.The pair helped New Zealand A move past India's total without losing a wicket. India A's bowlers struggled to find a breakthrough for much of the innings, despite the efforts of Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi and Mukesh Choudhary.Mukesh finally broke the opening stand when he trapped Mariu leg-before-wicket in the 39th over. The New Zealand A captain departed for 76, giving India A a much-needed breakthrough.Nabi then turned the closing stages of the day around with two wickets in two balls. He first bowled Lennox for a duck before trapping Robinson leg-before-wicket off the next delivery.The quick strikes left New Zealand A at 133/3, but Heaphy and Boyle survived the remaining deliveries to take the team to stumps at 135/3.India A will look to build on the late wickets when play resumes on Day 2. However, New Zealand A remain 22 runs ahead with seven wickets in hand.India A: 113 all out in 39.3 oversYash Rathod 44 not out, Devdutt Padikkal 32; Simon Keene 5/24, Zak Gibson 3/29.New Zealand A: 135/3 in 41 oversRhys Mariu 76, Curtis Heaphy 37 not out; Auqib Nabi 2 wickets, Mukesh Choudhary 1 wicket.New Zealand A lead by 22 runs.

Former West Indies all-rounder Kieron Pollard will take charge of Mumbai Indians as head coach ahead of IPL 2027. The five-time IPL champions announced the appointment on Saturday, with Pollard replacing Mahela Jayawardene Pollard has been working as Mumbai Indians' batting coach for the past few seasons. The franchise has now promoted him to the top coaching role, continuing its long association with the former West Indies T20 captain."Mumbai Indians are pleased to announce the elevation of Kieron Pollard to Head Coach, extending one of the most enduring player-to-coach associations in cricket," MI said in a statement.Mumbai Indians said Pollard's appointment was part of their plan to build on the team's success, develop young players and maintain their winning culture."Pollard's appointment reflects Mumbai Indians' commitment to building on the team's legacy while continuing to develop talent, strengthen its culture and pursue excellence on and off the field.""His leadership will be rooted in the experience of having been part of MI's most successful years, alongside the ambition to shape the team's next chapter," the franchise said.MI are among the most successful teams in IPL history, having won the title five times.However, their last championship came in 2020. One of Pollard's biggest challenges will be to help the team end its title drought.Pollard said Mumbai Indians had played a major role in his career and that he understood the responsibility of leading the team."MI has been a huge part of my life and career, and the bond I share with this team, the players and the Paltan means a great deal to me," Pollard said in a statement shared by the franchise."Having experienced this journey as a player and then as a coach, I understand what Mumbai Indians stands for and the responsibility that comes with representing the Blue and Gold," he added.The 39-year-old has played in franchise T20 leagues around the world. In the IPL, however, he represented only Mumbai Indians, from 2009-10 until his final appearance in the 2022 edition.Pollard also represented MI New York in Major League Cricket this year.In 189 IPL matches for Mumbai Indians, Pollard scored 3,412 runs at an average of 28.67 and a strike rate of 147.32. India A's star-studded batting line-up suffered a stunning collapse against New Zealand A, managing just 113 runs in the first innings of the opening unofficial Test at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval in Lincoln on Saturday.On a grass-covered pitch offering assistance to the fast bowlers, the Dhruv Jurel-led side had no answers to New Zealand A's disciplined attack. Five Indian batters failed to open their accounts, while the top order struggled to build partnerships. Yashasvi Jaiswal , Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan and Dhruv Jurel were expected to provide a strong start, but the experienced group failed to deliver. Rahul was dismissed for a duck after facing eight balls, edging Fraser Sheat behind the stumps. Jaiswal managed only 17 off 45 balls before Zak Gibson ended his stay.India A's problems did not end with Rahul and Jaiswal's dismissals. Padikkal scored 32 off 77 balls but struggled to turn his start into a substantial innings. His slow knock did little to lift the scoring rate as wickets continued to fall at the other end.Sudharsan, another batter expected to make an impact, departed for a duck after facing 13 deliveries.Captain and wicketkeeper Jurel managed just one run before falling to Simon Keene.Washington Sundar also failed to open his account, leaving India A reeling at 58/6. The visitors' inability to build partnerships or counter the movement generated by the New Zealand A pacers made for a deeply disappointing batting display.Keene was the standout bowler, finishing with five wickets for 24 runs in 11.3 overs. Gibson claimed three wickets for 29 runs, while Sheat and Kristian Clarke picked up one wicket each.India A lost their last five wickets for just 55 runs.Amid the collapse, Yash Rathod was the only batter who looked comfortable taking the attack to the opposition. He remained unbeaten on 44 off 49 balls, striking three fours and three sixes.As partners continued to depart, Rathod refused to let the innings fade away quietly. He scored the bulk of the runs in a last-wicket partnership with Mukesh Choudhary, helping India A cross the 100-run mark.Choudhary, however, contributed nothing with the bat before becoming Keene's fifth victim. Rathod's late counterattack could not hide the failures that had left India A in such a precarious position.India A's total of 113 leaves their bowlers with a difficult task. With the pitch continuing to offer assistance to the pacers, they will need early wickets to prevent New Zealand A from gaining a firm grip on the match.

Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf has explained his role alongside Shaheen Shah Afridi and Naseem Shah , saying their main job is to take important wickets and help the team win matches.Speaking to the media in Lahore, Rauf highlighted the importance of teamwork as Pakistan look to continue their strong performance in the ongoing ODI tri-series.“My role, along with Naseem and Shaheen, is to take wickets for the team. This is a team game, and everyone is supporting one another,” Rauf said.He also praised Shaheen’s presence in the bowling attack, saying his inclusion gives Pakistan an added advantage.“Having Shaheen in the team is always beneficial,” he added.Pakistan have started the tri-series well, winning their opening matches against Sri Lanka and England. Rauf said successfully defending a total of 300 runs was encouraging, but teams now need to score more runs because modern-day cricket has become more aggressive.“Defending 300 runs is a good sign. Our effort is to ensure that the bowling unit continues to perform well. When teams are scoring more than 300 or 400 runs, we also have to think about posting totals of 350 and defending them,” he said.Rauf also stressed that taking wickets during the middle overs is important to stop opposition batters from scoring freely and building strong partnerships.“You have to take wickets in the middle overs. Wherever you play in the world, runs are scored because cricket has changed,” he remarked.Rauf believes fast bowlers remain a major weapon in modern cricket. He said he is working on improving his fitness and speed to become more effective for Pakistan, while keeping his attention on performances rather than criticism.“A fast bowler is an X-factor in today’s cricket. I continue to work on my fitness and pace so that I can give people fewer reasons to talk,” he said.The pacer also backed Pakistan batters Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman to deliver important contributions in the remaining matches.After beating Sri Lanka and England, Pakistan will return to action against England in the fourth match of the tri-series at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium on Sunday, following a two-day break.The team will aim to maintain its winning momentum with strong performances from both its batting and bowling units.

Article Title: Will Ishan Kishan's injury be Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's gain? 15-year-old in contention for 2nd T20I vs New Zealand
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (BCCI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

One game into India’s tour of New Zealand and the familiar fitness concerns have already surfaced. Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday after sustaining a low-grade right adductor strain during the series opener on Thursday. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak revealed that Ishan was pushed down the order in the first T20I because of the injury. While a BCCI statement said the medical team is monitoring his progress, no timeline has been given for his return. Uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra was added to the squad as cover.The setback could finally pave the way for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who has spent the last nine matches on the sidelines. The team management, led by head coach Gautam Gambhir, has resisted calls to fast-track the 15-yearold despite the clamour around his talent. With uncertainty over Ishan’s recovery, however, the teenager may now get an opportunity in conditions far more challenging than those at home.Sooryavanshi attended an optional training session on Friday alongside Abhishek Sharma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Varun Chakravarthy, Shivam Dube and Kuldeep Yadav.Under Kotak’s watchful eye, he spent considerable time in the nets, a clear indication that the team wants him ready if needed. If the team management decides to veer away from their template of playing eight batters and field a spinner, Sooryavanshi may have to wait.Few young cricketers in recent years have generated as much excitement a s Sooryavanshi. His exploits in the IPL and age-group cricket have fuelled expectations, with fans, experts and social media all eager to see him in India colours more regularly. Yet the management feels patience will benefit him more than premature exposure. The challenge in New Zealand will be significantly different: larger grounds, movement off the pitch and through the air, and a minuscule margin for error. The examination could be sterner than what he has encountered so far.Kotak believes the teenager has already matured since first joining the national setup. “Now, he is much more mature. He understood why he is not playing. He has never complained. He is working on his fielding and fitness and is constantly observing others’ batting. The lessons you learn at this level are very different, and he has to absorb those too,” Kotak said.While acknowledging the popularity surrounding the youngster, Kotak cautioned against allowing public sentiment to dictate team selection. “Everyone likes him. The public likes him. Social media likes him. The team likes him. But you can’t make changes in the XI just because people like a player. He will learn a lot once he starts playing, but initially there was too much hype around his place in the side,” he said.“I genuinely felt that wasn’t good for the player either. For a 15-year-old, everyone saying he must play doesn’t leave him much space. He is still very young. It’s unfair on other players who are performing as well. People involved in cricket should think whether they are helping or simply creating noise.”Sooryavanshi has already captured the imagination of fans through his IPL exploits. If selected, the next step will be proving he can thrive when the conditions are far less forgiving.
Article Summary: Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday after sustaining a low-grade right adductor strain. Uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra was added to the squad as cover. The setback could finally pave the way for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who has spent the last nine matches on the sidelines.

Pratika Rawal scored her third ODI century while Shree Charani claimed career-best figures of 4/23 as India defeated Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the opening match of the three-ODI series in Vadodara on Friday.Zimbabwe were bowled out for 197 despite a half-century from Beloved Biza, with Charani and Kranti Gaud (3/42) leading India's bowling effort. Pratika then guided the chase with an unbeaten 100 as India reached 200/1 in 27.1 overs to take a 1-0 lead in the series.Pratika struck 15 fours in her 100 not out, scoring at a strike rate of over 100. The right-hander relied on shots along the ground and did not take unnecessary risks while batting on a pitch that offered little assistance to the bowlers.Pratika's opening partner Mandhana scored 32 before being caught by Biza at long-on off Olinder Chare in the 16th over, ending a 94-run opening partnership.Shafali, who came to bat at No. 3, continued her attacking approach and remained unbeaten on 64 off 33 balls, hitting five fours and four sixes.Earlier, Charani helped restrict Zimbabwe to 197 on a batting-friendly pitch at Kotambi. The left-arm spinner dismissed openers Modester Mupachikwa, who scored 25, and Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano (21) before returning to remove Nyasha Gwanzura (13) and Michelle Mavunga (29).Kranti Gaud supported Charani with three wickets for 42 runs as India kept Zimbabwe from building substantial partnerships. Biza was the visitors' top scorer, making 62 off 92 balls with five fours. She held one end together during the innings.India's bowling effort was, however, accompanied by several fielding errors, including dropped catches.In the third over, Mugeri-Tiripano edged a delivery from Gaud while attempting a drive outside off stump, but wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh failed to hold on to the catch.Mupachikwa offered another chance in the eighth over when she attempted to pull a wide delivery from Gaud and edged it towards Deepti Sharma at second slip. The India vice-captain tried to take the catch with a reverse cup, but the ball popped out of her hands.Mavunga also benefited from a dropped catch while scoring quick runs. She made her ODI debut against New Zealand in Queenstown in February 2022, scoring four off 14 balls.She found her rhythm in the next two matches of that series, scoring 49 off 50 balls and 61 off 41 balls. However, those three matches remained her only ODI appearances, in which she scored a total of 114 runs.In 17 T20Is, Meghana scored 258 runs at a strike rate of 102.78, including one half-century. She scored a half-century in both the ODI and T20I formats during her international career.Meghana also played three seasons of the WPL, beginning with Gujarat Giants before joining RCB, where she spent two years. She was part of the Bengaluru franchise's title-winning squad in 2024. Her last appearance in the league came during the 2025 season.

Teenage Indian para swimmer Ravi Budigina won his third medal at the Asian Para Games 2026, claiming bronze in the men's 50m freestyle S13 event in Nagoya on Thursday. Article Title: Brazil’s Igor Thiago lost his father at 13, worked as a garbage collector and bricklayer, and vowed to lift his family out of poverty before earning his first World Cup call-up in 2026
Article Text:
Igor Thiago lost his father at 13, worked as a garbage collector and bricklayer, and rose to earn Brazil’s 2026 World Cup call-up/ Image: Instagram

The Weight of the World on a Child’s Shoulders

The Fire Ignited and the Winding Path to Europe

The Historic Redemption and the Call of the Seleção

The Crucible of the World Stage and Beyond

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The glamorous, high-stakes theater of the English Premier League often obscures the raw, human battlegrounds where its most resilient stars are forged. In the spring of 2026, a towering Brazilian striker captured the imagination of the footballing world by completing an extraordinary, tear-stained ascent to the pinnacle of international sport. Long before he wore the famous yellow jersey of the Seleção, this young man endured a childhood of unimaginable deprivation and profound grief that would have broken lesser spirits. His narrative is not merely one of athletic triumph, but a deeply moving testament to a sacred promise made to a grieving mother under the scorching sun of South America.The story begins in Gama, a federal district in Brazil, though the young boy would spend his formative years navigating the unforgiving streets of Cidade Ocidental, a municipality plagued by devastating poverty and high crime rates. Life took a catastrophic turn when he was just thirteen years old, as his father passed away suddenly and stripped the household of its primary provider.Reflecting on this foundational tragedy, the forward would later recount the raw reality of his childhood to FIFA, stating, “My father passed away when I was 13. I started working at a street market carrying fruit. I also worked as a bricklayer. I had several jobs before becoming a professional footballer and getting the chance to play abroad.”This sudden tragedy plunged his single mother, Maria Diva, and his siblings into an immediate, terrifying financial crisis that threatened their very survival. Overnight, the young boy felt the immense, crushing weight of needing to help his family put food on the table. He spent his early teenage years balancing his schoolwork with grueling, hazardous manual labor that tested the limits of his physical endurance.To ensure his family did not starve, he worked exhausting, long shifts around garbage trucks as a refuse collector on the streets of his community. He also worked as a bricklayer's assistant, carrying heavy blocks and mixing mortar on local construction sites under the intense, unforgiving Brazilian heat. On other days, he could be found working as a market carrier, hired to transport heavy crates of fruit and vegetables on his aching back for minimal pay.Despite his love for football, his circumstances made pursuing the sport almost impossible because he could rarely afford proper boots, and traveling to trials placed a massive financial strain on his struggling mother. He faced repeated, heartbreaking rejections from various youth academies across Brazil, who routinely deemed him too raw or technically unpolished for their ranks.Looking back on those brutal early years from the luxury of his modern career, his profound reflection on those struggles shows how deeply they grounded his character. “It helped shape me as a man and as a person. I learned to appreciate both the smaller and the bigger things in life. Today, I can see how privileged I am to have what I have,” he said on the club’s website.During these dark moments of severe self-doubt, he famously looked at his mother and made a solemn promise that he would become a professional footballer to lift them out of poverty so she would never have to struggle again.His fierce determination was fueled by an immense love and admiration for the woman who sacrificed everything, working tirelessly to provide comfort even in the midst of extreme destitution. “I’m incredibly proud of my mother. No matter how difficult things were, she always made sure we had not just the basics, but good things as well. She is the strongest woman in the world,” he said. Looking at the lasting impact of his hard-fought success on the people he loves most, he beautifully added, “I’m proud to have helped my family and the next generation access things previous generations never had, because they had virtually nothing. ”While his mother worked grueling hours as a street cleaner, the family frequently dealt with severe poverty where they literally had no money for food. Throughout these trials, his older brother Maycon, who was fifteen years older, served as the primary reason he ever became a football player. Growing up, the future star did not even like football all that much, as it was Maycon who was widely considered the true athlete and the "footballer of the family".Maycon played a massive role in shaping his younger brother's life by forcing him to sit down and watch Premier League matches every single weekend, where the exploits of Manchester United and Cristiano Ronaldo inspired him to take the sport seriously. Furthermore, his entry into organized youth football was entirely thanks to Maycon, who was already playing for a local academy team called Gremio Ocidental. Because of Maycon’s connection and presence at the club, the coaches agreed to take a chance on the raw teenager, providing the crucial footprint that allowed him to be scouted by Verê Futebol Clube at the age of seventeen.This opportunity eventually caught the attention of Brazilian giants Cruzeiro, where he signed his first youth contract and made his professional debut in 2020. However, his time in Brazil's Série B proved to be turbulent and plagued by depression, forcing him to seek a fresh start through an unorthodox route to European football.He first rebuilt his career in Bulgaria with Ludogorets Razgrad, where he scored twenty-one goals and won consecutive domestic titles before moving to Belgium. His career truly exploded onto the broader European radar with Club Brugge, where he netted an incredible twenty-nine goals across all competitions during the 2023–24 campaign.His spectacular form in Belgium prompted Brentford F.C. to complete a club-record thirty-million-pound transfer in July 2024 to bring the striker to England. His initial adaptation to the Premier League was nearly derailed by a severe meniscus injury and a subsequent knee infection, limiting him to just eight goalless appearances in his debut season. However, the 2025–26 campaign saw him orchestrate a historic redemption arc under the guidance of manager Keith Andrews.Filling the void left by departing forwards, he became a lethal force in the Premier League by scoring nineteen league goals and twenty-two total goals by the spring, which later increased to an incredible twenty-two Premier League goals and twenty-six goals in all competitions. This remarkable tally broke Roberto Firmino's long-standing record for the most goals scored by a Brazilian in a single Premier League season.This historic scoring run transformed the stadium atmosphere, embedding the forward deeply into the folklore of the West London club. Every time Thiago scores for Brentford, the Bees fans burst into a chant inspired by Spandau Ballet’s Gold, as the closing line of the verse echoes around the stadium: “Always believe in Thiago!” It remains an incredibly fitting tribute from the stands, not least because unwavering belief has been the definitive key to his entire journey from the construction sites of Brazil to the peak of English football.On March 16, 2026, sitting right behind Erling Haaland in the Golden Boot race, he received his ultimate reward when head coach Carlo Ancelotti handed him his maiden senior call-up to the Brazilian national team. Just hours after his selection was announced to the world, he celebrated on the pitch by netting a brilliant goal against Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. When the official phone call arrived, Maycon, Samuel, Junior, Ranielly, and their mother were all gathered together to share in a tearful, emotional celebration of a journey they had built through shared hardship.Prior to this milestone, he had bared his soul to TNT Sports regarding the profound weight of this potential moment, declaring, “It’s my biggest dream. To wear my country’s shirt, to represent my country at the World Cup, it would show me that everything I’ve achieved and everything I’ve become… it’s because of God.”He made his senior international debut against France shortly thereafter; known widely across England as Brentford’s "penalty king," Thiago brought that signature, cold-blooded efficiency straight to the national team by famously taking the ball from Endrick to convert a pressure-filled penalty, before scoring his second international goal just days later in a three-one victory against Croatia, with both iconic moments taking place during the high-profile pre-World Cup international friendly window in March.By the time the summer of 2026 arrived, the striker had fully realized his lifelong dream by earning a coveted spot on Brazil's final squad for the FIFA World Cup, bringing his total international record to five caps and two goals. However, the tournament in North America did not follow the fairy-tale script that his domestic season had promised.Carlo Ancelotti surprised many by naming him in the starting lineup for Brazil’s opening Group C match against Morocco at MetLife Stadium, but the striker struggled immensely against a rigid defense. He squandered a massive early chance created by a Vinícius Júnior cross, recorded only sixteen touches, and looked visibly heavy in his hold-up play before being substituted in the sixty-second minute. Following that ineffective debut, he was dropped to the bench and did not feature for a single minute during the rest of the tournament, which saw Brazil suffer a premature exit in the Round of 16 against Norway.Now, in October 2026, months have passed since that grueling summer, and the heavy criticism from passionate Brazilian fans has undeniably dented his confidence. This international hangover contributed to a noticeably slow start to his current 2026–27 Premier League campaign with Brentford F.C., where he is working hard to rediscover his clinical edge.His post-World Cup club statistics reflect this demanding period of transition, as he has managed to register just 2 goals and 1 assist in 9 total appearances for the 2026–27 season across all competitions. While he has primarily featured as a starting forward in their Premier League campaign, starting all seven matches he has played while contributing one goal and one assist, he has also added another goal from two substitute appearances in the EFL Cup, bringing his total playing time to 664 minutes on the pitch.Yet, remembering the promise he made to Maria Diva during their darkest days of destitution, the 25-year-old striker remains optimistic about his upcoming fixtures and long-term future. Despite the emotional setback on the world stage, Thiago continues to draw strength from the purpose he finds beyond football.Reflecting on how the sport has changed his life, he said, “Football has transformed my family and everything around me.”His responsibilities at home have also helped him navigate the pressure and scrutiny surrounding his World Cup experience. With two children looking up to him, Thiago sees fatherhood as a powerful source of motivation. “I’ve grown stronger because I have two children who see me as an inspiration and a role model,” he explained. “That pushes me to improve. It motivates me to keep going. It’s made me a better son, a better husband and a better father.By grounding his professional ambitions in his role as a husband and father, the forward has found a way to process the disappointment and look ahead. He believes the World Cup experience has broadened his perspective, and remains determined to build on it, insisting that “this is just the beginning” of his international career.
Article Summary: Igor Thiago lost his father at 13, worked as a garbage collector and bricklayer, and rose to earn Brazil’s 2026 World Cup call-up. His narrative is not merely one of athletic triumph, but a deeply moving testament to a sacred promise made to a grieving mother under the scorching sun.

However, he returned to the dugout for Bayern's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday.After the match, Kompany admitted that he had tried to carry on despite being unwell and had ignored the signals his body was giving him.The Bundesliga leaders, who drew 2-2 at home against Arsenal in the Champions League earlier this week, are due to travel to Freiburg on Sunday.Bayern are scheduled to face Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday. The club said Kompany's coaching staff would oversee training and match-related activities while he remains under medical care.
Article Summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany hospitalised after collapsing. The 40-year- old was observing a training session when the incident occurred. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said his health was the club's top priority. Bayern are scheduled to face Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

Article Title: Will PSG’s 10 nominated players be forced to miss Ballon d’Or? Why Sunday’s Lyon clash is rescheduled to coincide on same night
Article Text:
PSG's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, center, is helped off the field by team staff after sustaining an injury during the Champions League opening phase soccer match between Paris Saint-Germain and FC Barcelona in Paris, Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026. (AP Photo/Thibault Camus)

Why PSG’s match with Lyon was postponed

The new date creates a Ballon d’Or dilemma

Injured nominees may have a different choice

Last year offers a striking precedent

Paris Saint-Germain's Ousmane Dembélé receives the 2025 Men's Ballon d'Or during the 69th Ballon d'Or awards ceremony at the Theatre du Chatelet in Paris, Monday, Sept. 22, 2025. (AP Photo/Thibault Camus)

What happens to the nominees now?

Could a sudden security postponement force Paris Saint-Germain’s brightest stars to watch their own Ballon d’Or coronation from the dugout?A last-minute police directive in Paris has triggered a bizarre logistical crisis, shifting PSG’s high-stakes Ligue 1 clash against Lyon to Monday night, placing it in a direct, agonizing bottleneck with football’s premier awards gala in London. While the club's fit nominees face a strict professional ultimatum to remain in France, a recent wave of injuries has created an ironic twist, potentially clearing the way for the squad's sidelined superstars to travel to the red carpet.Originally scheduled to host Lyon at the Parc des Princes on Sunday, October 25, at 8:45 p.m. local time, Paris Saint-Germain will instead play on Monday, October 26, at 8:30 p.m.The Ligue de Football Professionnel (LFP) confirmed the shift on Friday, stating that it "acknowledges the order issued by the Prefecture of Police prohibiting the holding of the PSG - Lyon match, scheduled for Matchday 8 of McDonald's Ligue 1, on Sunday, October 25, at 8:45 p.m., and has decided, in agreement with Ligue 1+, to reschedule the match for Monday, October 26, at 8:30 p.m."This late scheduling change comes as French authorities brace for a substantial security operation over the weekend. Law enforcement resources have been heavily stretched by nationwide demonstrations following a wave of severe unrest on October 17, when rioting and looting swept through Paris and other major cities, causing widespread damage to public buildings and private businesses.Compounding the strain on police resources is Sunday’s high-profile NFL regular-season game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints, hosted at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis—just ten kilometres from the Place de la Bastille, where massive weekend protests are expected to converge.As a result, France’s domestic sporting schedule has faced widespread disruptions. Local authorities previously requested that Toulouse’s fixture against Troyes be pushed from Saturday to Sunday, while both Marseille and Lille reported that their official club merchandise stores had been targeted and looted during the prior weekend's violence.The rearranged Monday night fixture carries massive sporting stakes on the pitch, bringing together two of Ligue 1’s early pacesetters. Defending champions PSG and rivals Lyon sit level at the top of the table on 14 points after seven matches, with Lyon holding the edge strictly on goal difference.The match now overlaps with the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, which is being held at the London Palladium on October 26. The gala marks the first time the award ceremony has taken place in England, with Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal among those hoping to unseat 2025 winner Ousmane Dembélé.PSG have a record 10 players on the men’s shortlist: Dembélé, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, Achraf Hakimi, Vitinha, Fabián Ruiz, João Neves, Willian Pacho and Ferran Torres. The club also has Warren Zaïre-Emery nominated for the Kopa Trophy, Matvey Safonov for the Yashin Trophy, Luis Enrique for Men’s Coach of the Year and PSG itself for Men’s Club of the Year.For players selected to face Lyon, the scheduling creates an obvious practical dilemma: the match in Paris clashes with the ceremony in London. Those involved are likely to prioritise their club commitments, but there has been no official confirmation of which nominees will attend the gala, whether PSG will make individual arrangements, or if the players will miss the ceremony altogether.Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes have been reported as injured and ruled out of the Lyon fixture. That could make attendance in London easier for them, although their travel plans have not been officially confirmed.The timing is particularly notable for Dembélé, who won the 2025 Ballon d’Or and is among the nominees again. His injury means he may be able to attend without missing the match, unlike fit teammates whose presence could be required in Paris.PSG encountered a similar scheduling problem last season, when heavy rain forced their Le Classique match against Marseille to be moved to Monday, coinciding with the Ballon d’Or ceremony at which Dembélé won.Dembélé was fit and important to the team, but PSG’s management gave him special permission to miss the rescheduled fixture so he could attend the gala. His teammates played without him and lost 1-0 to Marseille, making the decision a consequential one on the pitch as well as a memorable moment in his career.This year’s circumstances differ because Dembélé is reportedly injured and unavailable for the Lyon match. He would not need the same dispensation to leave the squad for London if he is unable to play, while fit nominees could face a more difficult decision. Whether PSG grants any exceptions, and which players ultimately attend, remains unconfirmed.The fit PSG nominees are likely to have their club duties to consider, while the injured players may have greater flexibility. Last year’s Dembélé arrangement shows that the club can make an exception for a major awards night, but it offers no guarantee that PSG will repeat that decision for other players.For now, the clash leaves the club balancing a top-of-the-table Ligue 1 fixture against an awards ceremony featuring an unusually large share of its squad. The final attendance picture will depend on PSG’s team plans, the players’ fitness and any decisions announced by the club or ceremony organisers.
Article Summary: Paris Saint-Germain's Ligue 1 match against Lyon has been postponed. The match was originally scheduled for Sunday, October 25, at 8:45 p.m. local time. The Ligue de Football Professionnel confirmed the shift on Friday, stating that it "acknowledges the order issued by the Prefecture of Police prohibiting the holding of the PSG - Lyon match" The match now overlaps with the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony in London.
